title: Step-Down Bridge Guidance Scheduling for Dual-CFG in Video-Audio Diffusion

contributions.purpose: Improve speech fidelity in joint video-audio diffusion where constant bridge guidance crowds out text-condition sensitivity in late denoising steps.
contributions.mechanism: Step-Down bridge guidance scheduling, a training-free modification for MOVA's dual-CFG that keeps high bridge guidance (s_B = 3.5) in early steps (k < 12) then cosine-ramps down to s_B = 1.5 in late steps (k >= 12).
contributions.evaluation: On Verse-Bench speech prompts it achieves 1.5% WER improvement over the constant baseline while preserving synchronization quality (AV-A within 1.2%).
contributions.source_quote: We propose Step-Down bridge guidance scheduling for dual-CFG video-audio diffusion, a simple training-free modification that improves speech fidelity by reducing bridge guidance in late denoising steps.

contributions.purpose: Explain mechanistically why constant high bridge guidance hurts speech fidelity.
contributions.mechanism: Norm analysis of guidance term dynamics across denoising steps under constant s_B = 3.5.
contributions.evaluation: Shows the bridge-to-text guidance norm ratio increases from 1.04 in early steps to 1.47 in late steps, indicating bridge guidance increasingly dominates the combined signal.
contributions.source_quote: We provide mechanistic evidence through norm analysis showing that bridge guidance dominates text guidance in late steps (ratio 1.47 vs 1.04), explaining why constant high s_B hurts speech fidelity.

contributions.purpose: Show that the temporal allocation of guidance strength, not just its values, determines speech fidelity.
contributions.mechanism: Controlled comparison of Step-Down against a constant baseline and against Step-Up (same guidance values in reversed order).
contributions.evaluation: Step-Down achieves 1.5% WER improvement with AV-A within 1.2%, and outperforms Step-Up by 1.9% despite identical guidance values.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that Step-Down scheduling achieves 1.5% WER improvement over the constant baseline while preserving synchronization quality (AV-A within 1.2%), and that timing matters—Step-Down outperforms Step-Up by 1.9% despite using the same guidance values.

self_declared_provenance.quote: While these works focus on single-condition CFG in image generation, our work extends timestep-dependent scheduling to dual-CFG in video-audio diffusion, where bridge and text guidance have distinct roles.
Our work focuses on optimizing the bridge guidance schedule in MOVA's dual-CFG framework.
Our work demonstrates that timestep-dependent guidance scheduling can improve generation quality in the audio domain, particularly for speech fidelity in joint video-audio synthesis.
